weekTitle: Robótica con Física, Eficiencia Extrema y Agentes de Trabajo: Los TOP Papers de la Semana
dateRange: Semana actual • Los más votados en Hugging Face
introduction: Esta semana la comunidad de Hugging Face ha puesto el foco en la eficiencia computacional y la interacción práctica con el mundo real. Analizamos desde modelos robóticos que entienden física sin latencia hasta técnicas que reducen el coste de cálculo en VLMs de difusión en casi un 65%.

podcast.speaker: Álvaro
podcast.text: ¡Hola a todos! Menudo menú tenemos hoy en el programa, Elvira. Arrancamos con PDRVLA, un modelo de robótica que aprende física del mundo real prediciendo características visuales futuras sin meter la latencia de generar vídeo en directo.

podcast.speaker: Elvira
podcast.text: ¡Impresionante, Álvaro! Generar vídeo en tiempo real para controlar robots era un cuello de botella brutal. Y hablando de vídeo, OmniShowcase soluciona el problema de la consistencia en 360 grados usando mapas de normales de superficie guiados por la geometría 3D del objeto.

podcast.speaker: Álvaro
podcast.text: Es genial cómo conectan la estructura 3D real con la difusión de vídeo. Y ¡ojo a esto! En el apartado de audio, Falcon nos trae extracción de voz en streaming recortando la latencia nada menos que 11 veces respecto a los modelos estándar.

podcast.speaker: Elvira
podcast.text: ¡Es que pasar de benchmarks sintéticos al ruido caótico del mundo real era una asignatura pendiente! Además, si nos vamos a mundos virtuales, Hy-Nomas nos permite controlar cámaras e instrucciones de texto de forma continua en un modelo de difusión de 8 mil millones de parámetros.

podcast.speaker: Álvaro
podcast.text: Totalmente de acuerdo, Elvira. Y para poner un poco de orden a toda esta ola de agentes, el trabajo sobre 'Work Agents' propone un marco de nivel de sistema para entender cómo ejecutan tareas digitales complejas de extremo a extremo.

podcast.speaker: Elvira
podcast.text: Una vuelta de tuerca muy necesaria para dejar de ver a los agentes como meros LLMs y empezar a tratar la persistencia del entorno. Y cerramos la semana con LOWN, que me ha dejado boquiabierta.

podcast.speaker: Álvaro
podcast.text: ¿Lo de mirar la imagen solo cuando hace falta en Diffusion VLMs? ¡Una genialidad pura! Evitar procesar el 90% de tokens visuales repetidos ahorra dos tercios del cómputo manteniendo casi el 100% de la precisión.

podcast.speaker: Elvira
podcast.text: ¡Exacto! Demuestra que a veces la innovación no es hacer modelos más grandes, sino hacer que piensen con más astucia cuándo necesitan ver y cuándo no. ¡Vamos al grano con las diapositivas!

slides.title: Robótica con Conciencia Física sin Latencia
slides.paperTitle: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
keyPoints: Módulo ligero de dinámicas físicas que predice RGB, profundidad y flujo óptico futuro.
Supervisión auxiliar mediante un World Model de vídeo congelado sin coste en inferencia online.
Rendimiento sobresaliente de hasta 99.3% de éxito en el benchmark LIBERO.
slides.takeaway: PDRVLA dota a los modelos de acción robótica de comprensión física del entorno evitando la latencia de generar vídeo en tiempo real.

slides.title: Vídeo 360° Consistente Basado en Geometría 3D
slides.paperTitle: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
keyPoints: Pipeline automatizado de síntesis de datos en trayectorias de cámara de 360 grados.
Condicionamiento geométrico mediante un tocadiscos de mapas de normales de superficie.
Superación del estado del arte en preservación de la identidad del objeto y consistencia 3D.
slides.takeaway: OmniShowcase resuelve la inconsistencia visual al rotar objetos 3D mediante el guiado explícito de normales de superficie.

slides.title: Extracción Causal de Voz Ultraligera en Tiempo Real
slides.paperTitle: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
keyPoints: Presentación de RealSSA, un benchmark realista con ruido complejo e interferencias dinámicas.
Arquitectura Falcon que realiza separación tiempo-frecuencia en un solo paso encoder-decoder.
Reducción del 91.9% en parámetros, 20.2x menos cómputo y 11.1x menor latencia en GPU.
slides.takeaway: Falcon permite extraer la voz de un hablante objetivo en tiempo real dentro de dispositivos finales manteniendo alta calidad acústica.

slides.title: Generación Interactiva de Mundos de Forma Libre
slides.paperTitle: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
keyPoints: Base de difusión de 8B parámetros que soporta texto libre y control continuo de cámara.
Atención causal consciente de la acción que restringe las instrucciones a su ventana temporal.
Prompt Enhancer que traduce el historial multimodal en condiciones estructuradas.
slides.takeaway: Hy-Nomas habilita la creación e interacción continua con entornos virtuales manteniendo coherencia histórica y espacial.

slides.title: Un Marco Unificado para Agentes de Trabajo Digital
slides.paperTitle: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
keyPoints: Perspectiva a nivel de sistema que combina modelos base y entorns de ejecución (harness).
Clasificación del trabajo digital en 5 formas según su alcance, persistencia y apertura.
Identificación de 5 familias de capacidades y técnicas de optimización conjunta.
slides.takeaway: Un marco conceptual clave para diseñar agentes capaces de ejecutar trabajo digital complejo, persistente y verificable.

slides.title: Ruteo Visual Inteligente para Difusión en VLMs
slides.paperTitle: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
keyPoints: LOWN decide dinámicamente en qué pasos de denoising procesar las imágenes.
Reutiliza predicciones anteriores si la predicción sin imagen coincide con la previa.
Ahorra el 64.7% de FLOPs de decodificación conservando el 99.6% del rendimiento original.
slides.takeaway: LOWN elimina el cómputo redundante de tokens visuales en modelos VLM de difusión sin necesidad de reentrenamiento.

papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
papers.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

papers.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
papers.summary: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. Early subject-to-video (S2V) methods condition on a single reference image and must therefore infer the subject's unseen appearance and geometry as the viewpoint changes. To address this limitation, recent methods extend S2V to multiple reference views, providing more information about the subject from different viewpoints. However, they do not explicitly specify the 3D structure that connects these observations. In addition, existing training data do not guarantee that viewpoint changes preserve the same underlying 3D subject. We present OmniShowcase, built on two components: (i) a fully automated data synthesis pipeline that produces training videos along diverse camera trajectories, with viewpoint variation driven by underlying subject geometry, even spanning full 360-degree orbits; and (ii) a geometry-conditioning method that provides the video model with a turntable of surface-normal maps reconstructed from the reference views without requiring temporal alignment with the generated frames. We construct Showcase-4K, a corpus of 3D-asset-based videos covering twelve camera motions across 88 trajectory configurations with reconstruction-derived surface-normal conditioning, and ShowcaseBench, a held-out evaluation set with the source meshes and camera parameters used to render each video. Experiments show state-of-the-art subject identity and 3D consistency while maintaining competitive video quality and motion. Project page: justin4ai.github.io/OmniShowcase

papers.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
papers.summary: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps. First, standard benchmarks fix the number of speakers at two and ignore the near-/far-field interference, reverberation, and sudden noise of real scenes. Second, high-performance causal architectures are too heavy for edge deployment. Lightweight alternatives try to reclaim capacity by repeatedly invoking a small separator, which offsets the savings. To address the first gap, we release RealSSA, a realistic AVTSE benchmark consisting of RealSSA-Sim and RealSSA-Real. RealSSA-Sim provides controllable simulated scenes with 1--5 dynamic near-field interfering speakers; scenes with far-field interference additionally include 10--15 far-field interfering speakers. RealSSA-Real provides a held-out real-recorded evaluation set. To address the second gap, we propose Falcon, a causal AVTSE method. Its Separator performs multi-scale time-frequency separation in a single encoder--decoder pass. We train Falcon with an encoder-space speaker contrastive loss. This loss suppresses near-field leakage at zero inference cost and transfers across backbones. Falcon achieves state-of-the-art extraction quality on RealSSA-Sim, LRS2-2Mix, LRS3-2Mix, and VoxCeleb2-2Mix. Compared with the causal AV-TFGridNet baseline, it cuts parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2 times, and GPU inference latency by 11.1 times. Code and demo are available at https://cslikai.cn/Falcon/.

papers.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
papers.summary: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.

papers.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
papers.summary: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

papers.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
papers.summary: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image. Visual token pruning methods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore propose LOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, so LOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average. LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/
